study.question: At the reduced prediction budget that preserves click AUC, does assigning residual capacity to cart and tower depth to fav recover more auxiliary predictive information than the reversed or symmetric assignments, and retain a measured prediction-cost advantage over the larger joint references?
study.hypothesis: Observation: round43 residual/shallow allocation R (tower42, residual2) yielded cart/fav AUC0.6769436039495349/0.6606106002636513, while depth/no-residual allocation D (tower44/32) yielded0.6643313472965207/0.6737168279059741. Dense counts204529/204533 are nearly equal. Both and the width-only/both-stage alternatives retained click AUC0.6671669182126774 and buy AUC0.7545928047791861. Mechanism hypothesis: cart and fav require different private nonlinear transformations of the same authorized frozen representation, so R for cart and D for fav can combine their complementary benefits without changing shared representation learning. This is provisional single-seed evidence, not established complementarity or a new architecture. Click preservation alone is insufficient: all reduced branches lose substantial auxiliary AUC relative to the larger buy-only incumbent (cart0.7867559970041751/fav0.7901027228512573) and to DIN. Broad embedding12 reduction (click0.6641111848808231) and shared projection reuse (0.6648248738234025) were negative trajectories; their speed/size changes do not justify transfer to this question. Round43 combined residual+depth was not uniformly best despite its similar budget. The proposed composition is the next bounded attribution step, not evidence that the full four-task objective has been preserved.

nearest_work.difference: Direct local ancestor. Keep its full template construction, masking, compression, click/buy and optimizer ownership; permit independent cart/fav residual presence and depth. Symmetric R/R must bridge exactly at the architecture and initialization level.

Closest replacement control. D/D bridges its tower44/32 and removed residual for both private tasks; mixed cells independently replace one head. The mixed and reversed assignments have exactly the same calculated parameter count and aggregate linear MAC count.

study.proposed_difference: Complete a two-by-two replacement design: cart allocation R or D crossed with fav allocation R or D. R means first tower width42, one Dice hidden layer, residual width2; D means tower44/32 with two Dice layers and no residual. New validated task-to-stage override maps change only cart/fav construction and the corresponding residual bypass. They consume no RNG and do not touch learned initialization order. Four standalone modules share the same executable implementation and differ only in literal CONFIG. R/R and D/D are exact source-lineage bridge controls, while R/D is the candidate and D/R is the equal-parameter/equal-linear-work assignment control. This is an incremental local capacity allocation experiment; novelty beyond the inspected references is unverified.
predictions: Prospective primary screen: click AUC of each admissible allocation must be at least0.6669669182126774 (incumbent0.6671669182126774 minus0.0002 absolute). Also report against the frozen original joint best0.666753547526167 and DIN0.6555440824200336; auxiliary mean never selects the click incumbent.

The preferred R/D assignment should improve the mean cart/fav AUC over both symmetric controls by at least0.003 absolute, with each private task within0.001 of its stronger symmetric allocation. The reversed D/R assignment should be worse in that private-task mean by at least0.005. These are prospective thresholds on exploratory validation, not significance claims.

If branch independence holds at the frozen seed, preferred cart/fav AUCs will approximately reproduce0.6769436039495349/0.6737168279059741 and buy/click will retain their reference values. Record absolute deviations rather than imposing this numerical prediction as an implementation requirement. Corresponding task-specific Logloss must not worsen by more than0.0001 versus its stronger symmetric source before calling auxiliary recovery useful.

R/R,D/D dense parameters should be204529 and204533; both mixed assignments204531. Embeddings remain31793216 and mixed total parameters31997747. Mixed private heads have38384 learned parameters and38032 linear multiply-accumulates per example; buffer/nonlinear costs are not matched. Host counts must confirm these calculations.

Prediction-cost utility must be measured, not inferred from counts: require at least2% reduction of both model-only p50 and p95 batch latency against a matched timing rerun of the larger buy-only incumbent and report the original joint best as a utility reference. No claim of beating the cheapest R/R control unless it actually lowers measured cost; an auxiliary/cost tradeoff is reported as such. Full-validation wall time and training wall time are separate endpoints. Historical timings are exploratory until matched repeats.
falsifiers: Failure of either primary preservation or measured prediction-cost gate rejects that candidate's efficiency utility; no reduced-capacity success is inferred from parameter arithmetic alone.
If preferred R/D fails the predeclared auxiliary gains or the equal-budget swapped assignment performs as well, the task-specific allocation explanation is unsupported at this operating point.

If symmetric bridges do not reproduce their own prior task metrics within0.00001 AUC at the same seed/protocol, or host counts/initial tensors disagree, treat this as a bridge or execution discrepancy before interpreting mixed cells. Retain costs and receipts; do not alter the frozen host contract.

If apparent improvements disappear under admissible paired repeats or matched timing, classify them as preliminary/noise. Paired user-cluster bootstrap is optional only if the host exposes authorized validation predictions; sample-level iid intervals are inappropriate.
Even if private allocation is supported, the observed auxiliary deficit versus the full model and DIN prevents any claim of preserving all four tasks or a general sequence-modeling mechanism.
